newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania sets 1997 external debt limit at $3.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Romania sets 1997 external debt limit at $3.2 bln.

text.p: The upper house of Romania's parliament, the Senate, has passed a bill setting the ceiling of the country's 1997 external debt at $3.2 billion, a parliament official said on Tuesday.
"Senators have voted unanimously the government decree which puts the external debt limit at $3.2 billion for this year," a Senate spokesman told Reuters.
In order to become effective, the bill, which cleared the lower Chamber of Deputies earlier this month, has to be approved by president Emil Constantinescu.

Under the bill, Romania's central bank and the finance ministry were entitled to raise and guarantee medium- and long-term loans from world capital markets to fund investment and restructuring and to enhance hard currency reserves.

Earlier this month, the Finance Minister said it planned to launch about 500 million DM in Eurobonds within one or two months. The central bank previously said it planned to raise up to $1.6 billion from international markets in 1997.
Since the 1980s Romania has been virtually absent from world capital markets, which it rejoined in 1995 with syndicated loans, followed by its first Samurai and Eurobond issues last year.
It won its first rating from major agencies -- a BB plus from Japan Credit Rating Agency, BB-minus by Standard and Poor's and Britain's IBCA and Ba-three by Moody's Investors Service.
Latest data put Romania's total foreign exchange reserves, including some 88 tonnes of gold, at $2.77 billion at end-January. External debt servicing is estimated at some $1.5 billion in 1997.
